To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Ce-rich precipitate could inhibit grain growth during annealing and thus improve the grain refinement and thermal stable behavior of spray-casted AZ9D magnesium alloys.
the grain refinement and thermal grain stability of spray-casted AZ9D+0.5Ce alloy are achieved by the addition of 1.5 wt% Ce, the formation of Mg12Ce particles, and their homogeneous distribution.
the addition of Ce can inhibit grain growth during the annealing process of spray-casted AZ 91D magnesium alloy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a Ce-rich precipitate on the grain growth of spray-casted AZ9D+0.7Ce alloy.
the grain refinement mechanism and thermal stability behavior in the spray-casted AZ-91D+0Ce alloy.
the grain refinement and thermal stabilization of spray-casted AZ9D+0.7Ce alloy by the formation of Mg12Ce particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grain growth could be suppressed by the addition of Ce and the resultant grain refinement was achieved by the combination of rapid solidification and Ce addition.
the adoption of rapid solidification and a non-equilibrium cooling rate can effectively suppress the grain growth during isothermal annealing.
the grain growth was effectively inhibited by the Mg12Ce phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of Ce is beneficial for the grain refinement of the spray-casted AZ9D magnesium alloy, which can be attributed to the formation of a solid solution and the suppression of the needle-like Al 11 Ce 3 phase with a high cooling rate.
the grain refinement and thermal grain stability behavior of the AZ91D+Ce alloy were attributed to the formation of a Mg12Ce phase.
the adoption of spray-casting and the addition of Ce are both beneficial in obtaining the desired microstructure and properties of magnesium alloy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of Ce to AZ91D magnesium alloys is an effective method to inhibit grain growth during annealing, which is attributed to the homogeneous distribution of Mg12Ce particles along the grain boundary.
a rapid solidification process and Ce addition are effective ways for inhibiting grain growth and improving the microstructural stability of AZ91D alloy.
the addition of Ce can improve the thermal stability behavior of spray-casted AZ 91D alloy, which is attributed to the formation of a Mg12Ce phase.
